name: ULTRA-VSR / 36K-48K Faithful Restoration Research Stack
purpose: International-observer-backed research framework for extreme-resolution video restoration with measurable fidelity, temporal coherence, reproducibility, provenance and no fabricated historical detail.

target.claimRule: Output pixel count is not proof of recovered factual detail.
target.fidelityPriority: historical/content fidelity > temporal consistency > OCR/text fidelity > perceptual quality > pixel count

newResearchCandidates.name: AVSR-Diff
newResearchCandidates.why: Scale-agnostic diffusion priors, continuous decoding, temporally-gated feature recurrence and scale-aware Fourier refinement; directly relevant to arbitrary target resolutions.

newResearchCandidates.name: SeedVR2
newResearchCandidates.why: One-step diffusion-transformer restoration with adaptive window attention and sequence parallel inference; official repo documents high-resolution VR and current compute limits.

newResearchCandidates.name: UltraVSR
newResearchCandidates.why: One-step diffusion VSR with degradation-aware restoration schedule, recurrent temporal shift and long-range temporally asynchronous inference.

newResearchCandidates.name: FlashVSR
newResearchCandidates.why: One-step streaming VSR using sparse attention and lightweight decoder; important efficiency comparator for extreme-resolution tiling.

newResearchCandidates.name: SparkVSR
newResearchCandidates.why: Keyframe/propagation strategy for extending restoration consistency across long videos.

newResearchCandidates.name: RealBasicVSR
newResearchCandidates.why: Established real-world VSR baseline for degradation-aware comparison.

newResearchCandidates.name: BasicVSR++
newResearchCandidates.why: Strong propagation and alignment baseline useful as deterministic/temporal comparator.

newResearchCandidates.name: VRT
newResearchCandidates.why: High-quality VSR/deblurring/denoising reference, but current official repository is not unrestricted for commercial production.

newResearchCandidates.name: RVRT
newResearchCandidates.why: Memory-aware recurrent restoration comparator; useful for long clips and tiling studies.

newResearchCandidates.name: DiffVSR
newResearchCandidates.why: Multi-scale temporal attention and temporal-enhanced VAE for fidelity and temporal consistency.

newResearchCandidates.name: AVSR-Diff
newResearchCandidates.why: Newest direct match to arbitrary-scale target generation and temporal stability.

newResearchCandidates.name: VSRELL
newResearchCandidates.why: Joint low-light enhancement and VSR; useful for degraded archival footage where illumination and resolution are coupled.

observerAndStandardsFramework.use: Use controlled subjective TV-image assessment for observer panels and device/display comparisons.
Use ACR/SAMVIQ/DMOS-style methodologies, high-quality reference stimuli, and documented test conditions.
Use archival-restoration principles: preserve original characteristics, entire frame, aspect ratio, version identity, provenance and research documentation.
Study open archival batch pipelines, ALTO/METS workflows and reproducible processing rather than treating commercial enhancement as a black box.
Where applicable, retain image/frame references, manifests and region-level provenance for auditability.

extremeResolutionRules: Never upscale in one monolithic allocation when tiled or progressive processing is safer.
Use overlapping spatial tiles and temporal windows to reduce seams and flicker.
Use multiple restoration engines as independent witnesses, not as blind sequential filters.
Where engines disagree on high-frequency detail, preserve uncertainty or prefer the conservative reconstruction.
Never use a generative frame as evidence for a fact absent from the source unless independently corroborated.
Preserve frame rate, aspect ratio and edit/version identity unless the project explicitly documents a justified transformation.
Keep source checksum, processing configuration, model identifiers, weights hashes and random seeds where applicable.
36K/48K is a delivery target, not a claim of native optical information.
A lower-resolution output with higher measured fidelity can outrank a higher-resolution output with hallucinated details.

observerPanel.principle: Independent observers should judge both visual quality and whether restoration remains faithful to the source.

globalSearchEvidence.name: FlashVSR

globalSearchEvidence.name: ITU-R BT.500
globalSearchEvidence.note: Current in-force methodology for subjective assessment of television images.

globalSearchEvidence.name: ITU-T P.910
globalSearchEvidence.note: Subjective multimedia video-quality assessment including SAMVIQ and high-quality reference-stimulus guidance.

globalSearchEvidence.name: FIAF Digital Statement Part III
globalSearchEvidence.note: Archival restoration ethics: preserve original frame, aspect ratio, version identity and provenance; restoration should remain faithful to historical characteristics.

doNotClaim: 36K/48K native detail from a lower-resolution source without evidence
a single model is universally best
benchmark score on generic video equals archival fidelity
open-source code automatically means open model weights or open training data
